exercise.title: Changes, one pair at a time
exercise.why: A change gets quick when the fingers leave together and land together, and that comes from making one change many times in a row, so each block is one pair of chords and nothing else.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear the chord. Change between Em and Am for about a minute, one strum on each, then rest your hand and go again.
Each round, lift all your fingers at once and put them down at once.

The same drill with E and Am. The chord boxes below show one shape in two places: all three fingers move across one string together.
Practice until the shape holds while it moves.

The same drill with A and D. Finger 3 stays on its string and slides up one fret, so let it lead and put the other two fingers down around it.
Go slowly enough that D is ready before you strum it.
